title: ADAPT for Science: A Multi-Agent System for Self-Evolving Scientific Optimization
title_zh: ADAPT for Science：一个用于自进化科学优化的多智能体系统

paragraphs.en: Scientific discovery often requires identifying a small number of high-performing designs in vast, constrained search spaces. This is difficult when evaluations are costly, feasible solutions are sparse, parameters are strongly coupled, and physical constraints are strict. Recent AI for AI methods can automatically improve algorithms and optimization procedures. However, general purpose approaches are not designed around scientific priors, physical constraints, and limited evaluation budgets. We introduce ADAPT for Science , a multi-agent framework that treats scientific optimization as two coupled decisions: where to search and how to search . ADAPT uses historical designs to identify promising and diverse initial conditions, progressively concentrates computation on favorable search directions, and evolves the optimization procedure from execution feedback. We evaluate ADAPT on the design of gravitational wave detectors using a differentiable physics simulator and eight unseen detector topologies. Under matched scientific evaluation budgets, ADAPT achieves a mean loss of 0.204 ± 0.101 0.204\pm 0.101 , reducing loss by 54.9 % 54.9\% relative to the best classical optimizer and by 62.2 % 62.2\% relative to the best general purpose agentic evolution baseline. ADAPT achieves the lowest loss on all unseen topologies among the evaluated baselines. ADAPT provides a step toward scientific optimization systems that continuously learn from prior experience and their own search outcomes.

paragraphs.en: Scientific progress often depends on finding a small number of useful solutions in vast and constrained design spaces. From drug discovery to gravitational-wave detector design, each candidate can be costly to evaluate, many parameters interact strongly, and feasible solutions may occupy only a small fraction of the search space. The central challenge is therefore not only to evaluate a candidate, but to decide what is worth trying next. This challenge becomes acute when optimization must proceed under a limited experimental or computational budget. Search performance depends not only on local parameter updates, but also on where the search begins, which prior experience is reused, which optimization procedure is applied, and how resources are allocated. These higher-level decisions are often fixed in advance or made manually, despite their substantial influence on the final solution. Gravitational-wave detector design provides a representative example. Detector sensitivity depends on many interacting continuous parameters subject to strict physical constraints. A poor initialization or an unsuitable optimization strategy can consume substantial computation before reaching a useful solution. At the same time, previous detector designs provide valuable experience that can guide future search. The problem is therefore not optimization from scratch, but how to reuse prior scientific experience, choose where to begin, and adapt the search strategy as new evidence becomes available.

paragraphs.en: AI has begun to automate parts of this process. Bayesian optimization and autonomous laboratories use previous evaluations to select promising candidates [ 25 , 31 ] , while scientific agents automate planning and experimental workflows [ 3 ] . These approaches primarily adapt the scientific candidate while the higher-level search procedure remains largely specified in advance. In parallel, recent program-search methods show that language models can improve algorithms through evaluator feedback [ 24 , 29 ] . These methods adapt the procedure itself, but do not explicitly model reusable scientific experience, target-dependent initialization, physical feasibility, and limited scientific evaluation budgets.
paragraphs.zh: AI已经开始将这一过程的部分环节自动化。 贝叶斯优化和自主实验室利用先前的评估来选择有前景的候选对象 [ 25 , 31 ] ，而科学智能体则将规划与实验工作流自动化 [ 3 ] 。 这些方法主要是在适应科学候选对象本身，而更高层的搜索过程在很大程度上仍是预先设定的。 与此同时，近期的程序搜索方法表明，语言模型可以通过评估器的反馈来改进算法 [ 24 , 29 ] 。 这些方法适应的是过程本身，但没有显式地建模可复用的科学经验、依赖目标的初始化、物理可行性以及有限的科学评估预算。

paragraphs.en: We address this gap with ADAPT for Science , a multi-agent framework for self-evolving scientific optimization. ADAPT treats the complete scientific search policy as the object of optimization and decomposes it into two coupled decisions: where to search and how to search . Historical scientific designs provide offline experience for selecting promising and diverse starting points and allocating evaluation effort. Online execution feedback is then used to evolve the optimization procedure itself. The resulting closed loop jointly adapts initialization, resource allocation, and optimization strategy to the scientific target. We evaluate ADAPT on gravitational-wave detector design using a differentiable physics simulator and eight unseen detector topologies. Under matched scientific evaluation budgets, ADAPT achieves a mean loss of 0.204 ± 0.101 0.204\pm 0.101 , compared with 0.452 ± 0.150 0.452\pm 0.150 for the strongest classical optimizer and 0.540 ± 0.263 0.540\pm 0.263 for the strongest general-purpose agentic evolution baseline. These results correspond to reductions in mean loss of 54.9% and 62.2% , respectively. ADAPT also achieves the lowest loss on all eight held-out topologies among the evaluated baselines. The results indicate that scientific optimization benefits from adapting the search policy itself rather than optimizing scientific parameters or optimization programs in isolation.

paragraphs.en: A complementary direction treats the optimization algorithm itself as the search object. Learned optimizers and symbolic program search demonstrate that optimization rules can be discovered from experience [ 2 , 5 , 11 , 36 ] . Algorithm discovery has further achieved improved computational procedures for tasks such as matrix multiplication and sorting [ 10 , 21 ] . More recently, large language models enable program and heuristic evolution through evaluator feedback, including FunSearch, EoH, ReEvo, and MCTS-AHD [ 24 , 18 , 33 , 35 ] . Related systems extend this idea to scientific equations, computational workflows, and automated optimizer evolution [ 29 , 7 , 1 , 17 , 27 , 15 , 26 ] . These approaches show that algorithms themselves can be optimized, but usually without target-specific scientific priors.

paragraphs.en: ADAPT connects these directions by treating the complete scientific search policy as the object of adaptation. Historical designs provide priors for where to search , while execution feedback evolves how to search . By jointly adapting initialization, resource allocation, and optimization dynamics, ADAPT enables efficient scientific optimization under physical constraints and limited budgets.
paragraphs.zh: ADAPT 通过将完整的科学搜索策略作为适应对象，把这些方向连接起来。 历史设计为在何处搜索提供先验，而执行反馈则演化如何搜索。 通过联合适应初始化、资源分配和优化动态，ADAPT 能够在物理约束和有限预算下实现高效的科学优化。

paragraphs.en: We construct a reusable experience library from historical gravitational-wave detector designs and optimization records. After cleaning, representation standardization, and transfer compatibility filtering, the design library contains 15,409 valid topology–design records, each pairing one topology with a compatible parameterized design and its evaluated performance. A separate baseline library contains ten established optimization procedures and their historical behavior. The former supplies candidate initializations, while the latter provides reference search behavior for policy evolution. Held-out targets and their outcomes are excluded from library construction and all subsequent strategy development.

paragraphs.en: A candidate policy may use historical attributes, transferred parameters, target evaluations, feasibility, constraint violations, and observed optimization progress to determine which candidates are evaluated, retained, or discarded and how budget is allocated among them. paragraphs.en: ADAPT is designed for scientific optimization with reusable historical experience, expensive evaluations, and explicit physical constraints. The present study focuses on gravitational-wave detector design, where a differentiable simulator provides controlled evaluation and a large historical design library. paragraphs.zh: ADAPT 专为科学优化而设计，其特点包括可复用的历史经验、昂贵的评估以及显式的物理约束。 本研究聚焦于引力波探测器设计，其中可微模拟器提供了可控的评估和庞大的历史设计库。 因此，这些结果证明了该框架在一个具有挑战性的科学领域的有效性，但尚未证明其在各科学学科间的普适性。

paragraphs.en: The method also depends on the quality and coverage of its experience library. This overhead is justified when scientific evaluations are sufficiently costly, but should be reduced for cheaper optimization problems.

paragraphs.en: Several extensions follow naturally. First, ADAPT can be evaluated on scientific problems with different search spaces, simulators, and physical constraints, including non-differentiable and experimental settings. Second, the experience library can be updated online so that successful solutions and optimizers become reusable knowledge for future targets. Third, more efficient strategy evolution could reduce the number of workflow–model evaluations through learned transfer, uncertainty-aware allocation, or meta-optimization. Finally, extending the independent validator to real experimental measurements would test whether self-evolving optimization remains reliable beyond simulation.

paragraphs.en: We introduced ADAPT for Science , a framework that treats the complete scientific search policy as the object of optimization. ADAPT decomposes this policy into two coupled decisions: where to search and how to search . Historical scientific experience guides target-specific initialization and resource allocation, while online execution feedback adapts the optimization procedure itself.
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出了 ADAPT for Science，一个将完整的科学搜索策略作为优化对象的框架。 ADAPT 将该策略分解为两个相互耦合的决策：在哪里搜索以及如何搜索。 历史科学经验指导面向特定目标的初始化与资源分配，而在线执行反馈则对优化过程本身进行自适应调整。

paragraphs.en: On eight held-out gravitational-wave detector topologies, ADAPT achieves a mean loss of 0.204 ± 0.101 0.204\pm 0.101 , reducing mean loss by 54.9% relative to the strongest classical optimizer and by 62.2% relative to the strongest general-purpose agentic evolution baseline under matched scientific evaluation budgets. paragraphs.en: We therefore base the main conclusions on the complete per-topology results in addition to aggregate means.

paragraphs.en: The present evaluation establishes ADAPT in one scientific domain: differentiable optimization of gravitational-wave detector designs with reusable historical experience and explicit physical constraints.
paragraphs.zh: 本次评估在单一科学领域中确立了 ADAPT：在可复用历史经验与显式物理约束下，对引力波探测器设计进行可微优化。

paragraphs.en: Several limitations should therefore be kept in mind.
paragraphs.zh: 因此，需要牢记几点局限性。

paragraphs.en: First, the effectiveness of target-aware retrieval depends on the coverage and quality of the historical experience library. Its benefit may decrease for targets that are far outside the observed design distribution.
paragraphs.zh: 首先，目标感知检索的有效性取决于历史经验库的覆盖范围和质量。 对于远离已观测设计分布的目标，其收益可能会下降。

paragraphs.en: Second, evolving both initialization and optimization procedures introduces development-time computational overhead relative to applying a single fixed optimizer.
paragraphs.zh: 其次，同时演化初始化与优化过程，相较于应用单一固定优化器，会带来开发阶段的计算开销。

paragraphs.en: Third, the present validator is simulation-based. Although the simulator provides a controlled differentiable scientific environment, the current results do not establish performance under real experimental noise, hardware imperfections, or non-differentiable laboratory feedback.
paragraphs.zh: 第三，当前的验证器是基于仿真的。 尽管该模拟器提供了一个可控且可微分的科学环境，但目前的结果并未证实在真实实验噪声、硬件缺陷或不可微分的实验室反馈条件下的性能表现。

paragraphs.en: Finally, ADAPT-Adam is an empirically discovered finite-budget optimizer. The present work does not claim a global convergence guarantee for the evolved update rule.
